As I look around, I see trays of dry compost under cracked glass, a sad state of affairs for a place meant to nurture life. I've just picked up a trowel, which I hope will be useful in restoring some order to this space. I've also taken a moment to examine the twine on the floor, a ball of it worn and frayed, but still possibly useful for some task or another.

As I stand in the cold, dark furnace, the weight of my trowel still clutched in my hand, I think back on the events that brought me here. I must have been searching for something or someone, but my memories of the journey are hazy. I recall walking through the nursery, where I picked up the trowel from the floor, examining its worn edge. The task of finding my way forward was far from clear.

Next, I picked up a piece of twine that had been lying on the ground. I've used twine before to tie up plants, but I couldn't imagine what I would need it for in this particular nursery. Maybe I'll use it to tie back some overgrown vines later.

As I looked around the room, I noticed a door to the north that seemed to lead to the furnace, and a colonnade that ran east. I decided to head in that direction, curious about what I might find.
